answer: Voting weight comes from proof-of-work history: an identity must complete 24 verified tasks over 14 epochs before it counts, and weight grows only with the square root of tasks done. A comet-fast farm of 50 clones pays 50 times the labor for under 7 times the influence, so each extra identity costs more per unit of power. Reviewers re-run a random 10% of tasks, and any summit of suspiciously perfect results, like a rehearsed sonnet, is slashed.
